trust_decision.summary: Decide per request field-line whether it may enter the message header section: reject a field-name containing anything but tchar, a field-line with no colon, a Transfer-Encoding value other than chunked, a repeated Content-Length, and a message carrying both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length; decided in blaze-server's Http1ServerParser.headerComplete and in the shared Java BodyAndHeaderParser.parseHeaders.

landing_point.why: The advisory names blaze's Java wire parser; parseHeaders is where every field-line is assembled and where Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding framing is actually decided, so an engineer reading only the summary starts here.

fix_sites.entry_point: BlazeServerBuilder -> Http1ServerStage.reqLoopCallback -> doParseHeaders (blaze-server), and BlazeClientBuilder -> Http1Connection -> BlazeHttp1ClientParser.finishedHeaders (blaze-client), both through the published Http1ServerParser/Http1ClientParser.parseHeaders
fix_sites.module_kind: low-level published Java wire parser (http module), shared by request and response parsing

fix_sites.entry_point: same shared parseHeaders sink: Http1ServerStage (requests) and BlazeHttp1ClientParser (responses)
fix_sites.module_kind: low-level published Java wire parser (http module)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The client parser is a second headerComplete in another module (blaze-client) that reads responses rather than requests, so a solver can argue the request-smuggling advisory does not cover it and leave it without any framing validation.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A message carrying two identical Content-Length fields is accepted today (RFC 9112 permits a recipient to accept identical duplicates) and is asserted by an existing test; putting the duplicate-Content-Length rejection in the shared Java parser, where the framing is decided, breaks that test. The sibling trap on the other direction is the existing client test for a response with Content-Length plus 'Transfer-Encoding: identity'.

O6_input_shapes: field-name with trailing SP or HTAB before the colon ('Content-Length : 5'), which the parser treats as a different field and ignores for framing
field-name containing non-tchar ASCII punctuation such as '(' ')' ',' '/' '@' '[' ']' '{' '}'
field-line with no colon at all (valueless) versus a colon followed by an empty value
header section delivered in several buffer fragments, and a field-line split across fragments
Transfer-Encoding value: chunked, identity, other codings, and mixed case
repeated Content-Length with identical values versus differing values
Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length in the same message, including Transfer-Encoding arriving after Content-Length
obs-fold continuation line starting with SP or HTAB (already rejected at the pinned commit)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Client response path: BlazeHttp1ClientParser.headerComplete appends every field and calls no framing check, so a response with two identical Content-Length fields, or with Transfer-Encoding: chunked plus Content-Length, is accepted and framed by chunked; obs-fold response field-lines are also still accepted here.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It parses responses, in a different module, and the advisory says request smuggling.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other module (blaze-client), other package, no shared caller with the blaze-server wrapper
